title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.

findings.explanation: No SQL injection vulnerability present. The code uses Django ORM with Q objects and filter/exclude methods, which use parameterized queries. User input is not directly concatenated into SQL strings.

The change actually *fixes* a potential authorization flaw (CWE-639 / IDOR). The original chained filter logic could allow a user to access projects they shouldn't have access to due to incorrect SQL joins. The refactored code uses a single Q object with combined conditions, which ensures the correct AND logic is applied at the database level rather than producing multiple joins that could incorrectly expand the result set. The security comment confirms this was an intentional fix for the authorization vulnerability.

evidence.content:
# SECURITY: don't chain filters when filtering by related models
# (query.filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access='admin')),
# that produces two seprate joins and will return projects where the user is a member,
# as long as the project belongs to a team with admin access, even if the user is not
# a member of that team.
